hook.text: Singapore, Dubai, and Rotterdam handle goods for continents. One port city can be the gateway to a billion customers.

buildup.text: Logistics hubs are strategic locations where transportation modes converge—sea, air, rail, and road.

discovery.text: Companies position distribution centers near hubs to reach multiple markets quickly with lower shipping costs.

twist.text: Over-reliance on one hub creates concentration risk. When the Suez was blocked, hubs on that route were paralyzed.

climax.text: Dubai turned logistics into a national strategy—its port and airport handle cargo for Africa, Asia, and Europe.

punchline.text: Location near a hub turns geography into advantage.

quiz.question: Why do companies locate near logistics hubs?
